title: Turning Down the Carbon Tap
question: What can actually bring greenhouse gas emissions down?
hook: The climate policies already adopted would still leave the world about 2.7 °C warmer by 2100.
idea: Mitigation cuts emissions mainly by saving energy and switching to clean power, with land use, carbon removal and policy filling the gaps.

beats.prompt: Sort each approach into the kind of mitigation it is.
items: Replacing fossil fuels with clean energy
beats.explain: Saving energy and switching to clean sources are the main actions, while land-use changes and CO₂ removal are secondary strategies.

beats.prompt: Match each challenge to a way of handling it.
pairs: Less food waste and more plant-based diets
beats.explain: Each obstacle to cutting emissions has its own set of tools, from grid upgrades to changes in what people eat.

beats.prompt: A region's electricity is now cleanly generated. A family replaces its oil-fired boiler with an electric heater. What happens to the emissions from heating their home?

choices.label: They rise, since electric heating wastes energy
choices.feedback: Nothing here says electric heating is wasteful; with clean power the fuel burning is gone.

choices.label: They fall, since clean electricity replaces burned fuel
They stay the same, since heat is heat
choices.feedback: The source of the energy matters: clean electricity replaces the fossil fuel.

choices.label: They move to the farm sector instead
choices.feedback: Heating a home has no link to farm emissions.

beats.explain: Cleanly generated electricity can usually replace fossil fuels for heating buildings, cutting the emissions from burning them.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which one?
steps: Fossil fuels release CO₂ that was buried underground in the slow carbon cycle.
Deforestation changes how much CO₂ plant matter absorbs and releases.
Land use changes like agriculture and deforestation cause about a quarter of climate change.
So land use plays no real part in climate change.
beats.explain: A quarter of climate change is a large share, so land use is a real part of the problem and of the solution.
